construct: HFE dysfunction reduces hepatocyte hepcidin upregulation. Low hepcidin fails to induce ferroportin internalization/degradation, so ferroportin remains active on enterocytes and macrophages, increasing dietary iron absorption and iron release into plasma.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: HFE C282Y homozygosity with high transferrin saturation, liver iron, diabetes, bronze skin, and MCP arthropathy indicates inadequate hepcidin signaling; persistent ferroportin activity increases iron entry into plasma.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Excess hepcidin and ferroportin loss cause iron restriction/trapping rather than classic HFE iron loading; transferrin reduction and DMT1 deficiency do not reproduce the HFE-hepcidin-ferroportin mechanism.
